note: WHAT EXPIRES, AND WHAT HAPPENS WHEN IT HAS. Each check names the table, the column holding the date the credential runs out, and how many days of warning are useful. `applies_when` narrows it to the rows the obligation is actually on — an exited employee's lapsed certificate is not a finding. `blocks` says, in words, what must not happen while it is lapsed, because a compliance screen that reports a date without saying what the date stops is a list nobody acts on. A row whose date is NOT SET is reported as not determined and never as compliant: 'no expiry recorded' and 'in date' are opposite facts and look identical in a count.

checks.label: DRA certification
checks.blocks: allocation of recovery work — the DRA certificate is the RBI-facing credential, and an agent working on a lapsed one is a finding against the bank as well as against us
checks.why: Sixty days of warning because a DRA refresher has to be booked, sat and certified, and none of that happens in a week.

checks.label: Police clearance certificate
checks.blocks: field visits and client-site deployment — most bank contracts require a current PCC on file for every agent they let near a customer
checks.why: Forty-five days because a PCC is issued by a police station on its own timetable, not ours.

checks.label: Bank authorisation letter
checks.blocks: collection on that portfolio — an agent calling a customer on an expired authorisation is doing it without the bank's mandate
checks.why: Thirty days: renewing is a request to the bank, and banks answer in weeks.

checks.label: Employee documents
checks.blocks: nothing on its own, but an expired identity or address document is the one somebody discovers during an audit rather than before it
checks.why: Thirty days is enough to ask for a replacement copy.
